predecessors.name: Portugal (Estado Novo and Third Republic)
predecessors.text: Portuguese Timor, the colony from which Fretilin 'unilaterally declared independence' on 28 November 1975

predecessors.name: Republic of Indonesia
predecessors.text: East Timor, which the last Indonesian troops left by 31 October 1999 and the UN then administered

ledger.x: 1975: Fretilin declares East Timor independent at Dili (28 November).
1976: East Timor passes to Indonesia (17 July).
October 1999: Indonesia leaves East Timor and the UN takes over.

20 May 2002: East Timor becomes independent as the Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, when the Constitution came into force and the UN recognised the independence; it joined the UN on 27 September 2002.

wars.name: Indonesian occupation of East Timor
wars.outcome: Indonesia invaded on 7 December 1975, annexed East Timor on 17 July 1976 and withdrew by 31 October 1999 after the UN-supervised referendum of 30 August 1999; the UN administered the land until independence on 20 May 2002.

certainty.note: The land border with Indonesia is the 1914 Permanent Court of Arbitration line, which 'remains the international boundary' (about 125 km); the Oecusse exclave sits inside Indonesian territory.
